report.summary: Chunk 5 of 10 of typegraph.py: defines private methods for bindings, star imports, alias module resolution, and candidate generation.
risks: _bare_candidates | medium | The method returns targets as set of tuples; the docstring says 'distinct (module, original name) pairs' but the code also includes alias.kind, alias.level in _dotted_candidates, inconsistency may cause confusion.

_dotted_candidates | medium | The method builds modules list but never uses it; the docstring mentions generating two readings for from imports, but the code does not show generation of the second reading (submodule vs type). The code is incomplete in this chunk.
todos: Check that _dotted_candidates uses the modules list or remove it; the code chunk ends before completion.

handoff.purpose: Defines private helper methods for import binding resolution and candidate generation.

symbols.name: _bindings
symbols.note: Returns a dict mapping local name to tuple of AliasImport for a given importer. Caches in self._binds and self._stars.

symbols.name: _star_imports
symbols.note: Returns tuple of star imports (AliasImport) for a given importer.

symbols.name: _alias_module
symbols.note: Computes the dotted module from an ImportFrom alias, handling relative levels.

symbols.name: _declared
symbols.note: Returns the node id for a qualname in a relative module, or empty string if not declared.

symbols.name: _bare_candidates
symbols.note: Returns candidates for a simple name import: node ids, saw_binding, saw_internal, targets set.

symbols.name: _star_candidates
symbols.note: Returns candidates from star imports for a given name.

symbols.name: _dotted_candidates
symbols.note: Resolves dotted names like head.mid.Leaf via binding of head.

claims.text: The dotted module an ``ImportFrom`` binding reads from. Relative levels are anchored exactly the way ``parse.resolve_python_imports`` anchors them, so the two never disagree about which package a ``from ..x import y`` means.
claims.why: The referenced function parse.resolve_python_imports is not in this chunk; the implementation of _alias_module appears to handle relative levels but we cannot verify the claim that it matches that external function.

claims.text: The membership test is the ONLY thing that mints a target: a name is never minted into a node for having been mentioned.
claims.why: The function checks if qualname is in self._tbf[rel] and only then returns a node id; otherwise returns empty string. It does not create nodes.

claims.text: Python binds the LAST import that executes, so two bindings that disagree about where the name comes from make the answer a property of the environment rather than of the source -- and picking the visible one would be a guess dressed up as a resolution. Two bindings that AGREE (the common ``if TYPE_CHECKING`` duplicate) are not a disagreement and still resolve.
claims.why: The docstring describes the design intent, but the code in _bare_candidates does not implement the logic to detect disagreement or agreement; it simply collects all bindings. The claim about resolution behavior is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: ``targets`` is the set of distinct ``(module, original name)`` pairs the bindings point at, and it is what makes the try/except case refusable even when only ONE of the two branches is a module we can see.
claims.why: The code builds targets as a set of tuples, but for 'import' aliases it adds ("module", alias.orig) which is a tuple of two strings, not a (module, original name) pair. For 'from' aliases it adds (module, alias.orig) which matches the description, but the inconsistency means the claim is not fully accurate.

observations.what: _bindings stores results in self._binds and self._stars, but _star_imports calls _bindings and then retrieves from self._stars.
_dotted_candidates builds a list 'modules' but never uses it; the code chunk ends before it is used.

In _dotted_candidates, the comment says two readings are generated for from imports, but the code only shows one path (the else branch). The generation of the second reading is not visible in this chunk.

The targets set in _bare_candidates includes tuples of different structure: for 'import' it's ('module', orig), for 'from' it's (module, orig). This inconsistency may affect callers expecting uniform tuples.
